name: 493. A price-affecting field nested inside an extra param is refused (nested price field)
description: Fork contract C4 (a price-affecting field is delivered or refused, never smuggled), TXE-7124. Local fixture regression, no live provider calls: start tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs, start an isolated gateway on tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json and run with providerErrorFixture=1; every case is skipped otherwise. Folders 430 and 434 pin that an extra param cannot supply a price-affecting field under its unified name or the vendor's own top-level name. Extra params are merged into the converted body object by object, so on a provider whose body holds price fields inside an object, an extra param named after that object added the nested field when the request left the unified one out: parameters.durationSeconds on a Veo video, generationConfig.imageConfig.imageSize on a Gemini image, voice_setting.speed on MiniMax speech. The vendor billed for a value no unified field showed. schemas.NestedPriceFields lists those paths per provider and operation, and the request worker refuses an extra param that sets one with 400 caller_unsupported_parameter naming the path as the caller spelled it, before a key is chosen. The names are compared the way a vendor that takes camelCase and snake_case reads them. Rows 1 to 7 are refusals on five providers, each asserting that the fixture received nothing. Row 8 is the control: a sibling in the same object that is not a price field still reaches the vendor beside what the converter wrote. Go pins the whole table: core's TestNestedPriceFieldsAreDeclaredAndRefused sends every price-affecting field through every provider's converter and fails when one lands on a nested path that is not listed (62 paths on bedrock, byteplus, elevenlabs, gemini, vertex, google-cloud-tts, minimax and replicate), so Bedrock, ElevenLabs and Vertex, which this fixture config cannot serve these rows for, are covered there.
